authority_references.title: 17 U.S.C. § 102 — Subject matter of copyright
authority_references.proposition_checked: Copyright subsists in original works fixed in a tangible medium; musical works and sound recordings are listed categories; ideas are excluded.

authority_references.title: 17 U.S.C. § 106 — Exclusive rights
authority_references.proposition_checked: Lists exclusive rights subject to statutory limitations; the sound-recording public-performance right is § 106(6), for digital audio transmission.

authority_references.title: 17 U.S.C. § 114 — Scope of sound-recording rights
authority_references.proposition_checked: Sound-recording rights are limited by statute; § 114(b) distinguishes recapture of actual recorded sounds from independently fixed sounds that imitate them.
limitations: Does not resolve composition rights, other causes of action, or every sample/interpolation dispute.

authority_references.title: 17 U.S.C. § 101 — Definitions
authority_references.pinpoint: Definitions of “joint work” and “work made for hire”
authority_references.proposition_checked: Defines a joint work through authorship and intent to merge contributions; gives two work-made-for-hire routes and a limited list for specially ordered/commissioned works.
limitations: Classification and authorship thresholds may require controlling case law; do not decide from labels alone.

authority_references.title: 17 U.S.C. § 201 — Ownership of copyright
authority_references.proposition_checked: Initial ownership vests in author(s); joint-work authors are coowners; a work made for hire treats employer/commissioning party as author subject to written contrary agreement.
limitations: Section 201 does not resolve every joint-owner licensing/accounting default.

authority_references.title: 17 U.S.C. § 204 — Execution of transfers
authority_references.proposition_checked: A transfer of copyright ownership other than by operation of law requires a writing signed by the owner or duly authorized agent.
limitations: This check does not decide whether a particular provision is a transfer, license, or enforceable agreement.

authority_references.title: 17 U.S.C. § 408 — Registration in general
authority_references.proposition_checked: Registration is not a condition of copyright protection.

authority_references.title: 17 U.S.C. § 411 — Registration and civil actions
authority_references.proposition_checked: Sets a registration/preregistration requirement before civil infringement action for U.S. works, with statutory exceptions and a refusal-of-registration procedure.
limitations: Do not calculate eligibility for a specific claim without work origin, dates, and procedural facts.

authority_references.title: 17 U.S.C. § 412 — Registration and certain remedies
authority_references.proposition_checked: Limits statutory damages and attorney-fee awards for specified pre-registration infringements, subject to exceptions including qualifying preregistration and a three-month post-publication path.
limitations: Exact eligibility depends on publication, effective registration, first infringement, preregistration, and other statutory facts.

authority_references.title: 17 U.S.C. § 115 — Mechanical licensing
authority_references.proposition_checked: Provides conditional licensing routes for reproduction/distribution of nondramatic musical works, including a blanket license for eligible digital music providers and covered activities.
limitations: No rate, notice, eligibility, usage, or reporting advice is provided here.

authority_references.title: 17 U.S.C. § 107 — Fair use
authority_references.proposition_checked: Lists illustrative fair-use purposes and four nonexclusive factors for case-specific evaluation.
limitations: The statutory factors do not predict an outcome; current controlling cases were not surveyed.

authority_references.title: U.S. Copyright Office Circular 30, Works Made for Hire (rev. Aug. 2024)
authority_references.proposition_checked: Explains the two statutory work-made-for-hire routes, commissioned categories, signed written agreement requirement, and that status depends on facts existing when work was created.
limitations: General guidance; statute and controlling cases govern.

concepts.title: Composition and sound recording are separate works
concepts.primary_question: Which asset is being licensed, cleared, registered, delivered, or assigned?

content.source_layer: The book treats a musical work and a sound recording as separate copyrightable categories and describes the composition as the musical notes/lyrics and the recording as the particular captured sounds.
content.application_layer: Make a rights map with one row for the composition and one for each master/version. Verify the actual grantor and rights for each asset.
content.current_law_layer: Title 17 separately lists musical works and sound recordings; sound-recording rights also have a distinct statutory scope.

claims.proposition: The book distinguishes the musical composition from the fixed sound recording; current Title 17 lists both as distinct categories and gives sound recordings a separately limited rights scope.
exceptions_or_qualifications: This confirms the asset distinction; it does not decide ownership or whether a particular use requires permission.

concepts.title: Copyrightable expression, fixation, and ideas
concepts.primary_question: What original expression is fixed, in which work, and what material remains an idea or method?

content.source_layer: Chapter 3 addresses originality, expression, fixation, and the exclusion of ideas; the contents identify these as separate requirements/topics.
content.application_layer: Identify the actual recorded/notated material and version. Do not treat a concept, genre, method, title, or sound alike observation as a copyright conclusion.
content.source_coverage: Chapter 3 substantive reading was selective; use the locator for the legal proposition actually cited.

claims.proposition: The current statute protects original works fixed in a tangible medium, lists musical works and sound recordings, and excludes ideas and systems from protection.

concepts.title: Authorship is a contribution question, not a role label
concepts.primary_question: What expression did the person create, and where is the evidence of that contribution?

content.source_layer: The book distinguishes sound-recording authorship contributions from job titles and notes that not every participant necessarily contributes authorship.
content.application_layer: Record composition contributions separately from performance, production, engineering, arrangement, and delivery services. Preserve demos, session notes, drafts, stems, and contemporaneous communications as evidence; none alone decides ownership.

claims.proposition: The book describes sound-recording authorship as potentially involving performers and production choices, while cautioning that contributions vary. This supports asking for contribution evidence, not assigning rights from role alone.
verification_needed: Apply current authorship and work-made-for-hire law to the exact facts.

concepts.title: Initial ownership and registration are different questions
concepts.primary_question: Who authored the work, and is the issue initial ownership, later transfer, or registration?

content.source_layer: The book states that initial ownership begins with the author, subject to statutory exceptions, and distinguishes ownership from registration.
content.application_layer: Trace authorship first, then any work-made-for-hire status, signed transfers, licenses, and later changes. A registration record or paid invoice does not replace this analysis.

claims.proposition: The source distinguishes copyright protection/initial ownership from registration; current §§ 201 and 408 place initial ownership with author(s) and state that registration is not a condition of protection.
exceptions_or_qualifications: Work-made-for-hire, transfers, other statutory rules, and the facts may alter who holds rights.

concepts.title: Joint authorship requires an evidence trail
concepts.primary_question: What copyrightable contribution and shared intent support the claimed joint work?

content.source_layer: The book discusses both intention to combine contributions and copyrightable authorship, and distinguishes those questions from service, ideas, and credit.
content.application_layer: Capture each contribution, when it was made, what others understood, and the version into which it was incorporated. Separate authorship classification from negotiated split documentation.

claims.proposition: The book discusses authorship and intent as separate joint-work issues; current § 101 defines a joint work through authorship and intent that contributions be merged, while § 201 makes joint-work authors coowners.
exceptions_or_qualifications: Do not decide authorship, relative shares, or licensing powers without controlling case law and the parties’ evidence.
verification_needed: Circuit-specific joint-authorship cases and any governing contract/state law.

concepts.title: Work made for hire is a narrow classification
concepts.primary_question: Which statutory route is asserted, and what facts and signed documents support it?

content.source_layer: The book separates employee work within scope from specially ordered/commissioned work that must fit a statutory category and satisfy formal requirements.
content.application_layer: Ask which route is asserted; identify the relationship, category, work, parties, signed instrument, date, and any alternative assignment. Do not accept a role label, contractor label, or payment as the result.
content.current_law_layer: Current § 101 and U.S. Copyright Office Circular 30 retain two distinct routes; Circular 30 says status turns on facts when the work is created.

claims.proposition: The source describes employee/scope and qualifying commissioned work as separate routes. Current § 101 and Circular 30 confirm employee work within scope or a statutorily listed commissioned category with express signed writing.
exceptions_or_qualifications: A role label or recital alone does not establish employee status, scope, qualifying category, timing, or validity.

concepts.title: Assignment, license, and administration must be distinguished
concepts.primary_question: Does the clause transfer ownership, authorize use, or appoint an administrator/collector?

content.source_layer: The book distinguishes transfers, exclusive licenses, and nonexclusive licenses and notes that rights may be divided.
content.application_layer: Mark the operative verb, right, asset, exclusivity, scope, territory, term, permissions, collection authority, and reserved rights. Administration and collection terms may be commercial/contractual and are not fully supplied by the book.

claims.proposition: The book describes transfers and licenses as different arrangements; current § 204 requires a signed writing for a transfer of copyright ownership other than by operation of law.
exceptions_or_qualifications: Classify the actual clause before applying the transfer rule; an agreement’s label is not dispositive.

concepts.title: Map rights to the actual use
concepts.primary_question: What exclusive right, limitation, permission, or reserved right is implicated by each use?

content.source_layer: The book organizes reproduction, derivative, distribution, public performance/display, and limitations in separate chapters.
content.application_layer: For each proposed use, map asset → act/use → territory → term → license/exception → responsible party → evidence. Do not assume one broad word such as “publishing” or “master” answers every dimension.
content.current_law_layer: Current § 106 lists rights subject to statutory limitations; §§ 114 and 115 include rights-specific qualifications.

claims.proposition: Current § 106 enumerates reproduction, derivative-work, distribution, public-performance and display rights, with a distinct digital-audio-transmission right for sound recordings, subject to statutory limitations.
exceptions_or_qualifications: Specific statutory exceptions and licenses can change the result; identify the actual act and asset.

concepts.title: File delivery does not answer rights
concepts.primary_question: Does the clause govern files and services, copyright, or both?

content.source_layer: The book distinguishes ownership of an embodied physical/digital file from ownership of the copyrights in the works contained in it.
content.application_layer: List masters, multitracks, stems, session/project files, exports, backups, and editable materials as delivery items; separately identify copyright ownership, license, access, confidentiality, and permitted exploitation.

claims.proposition: The source distinguishes possession of a file/object from ownership of the copyright embodied in it; use that distinction as a contract-review question.

concepts.title: Registration and remedies need separate date facts
concepts.primary_question: Is the question copyright existence, an infringement suit, or availability of particular remedies?

content.source_layer: The book has a chapter on registration and a separate chapter on infringement remedies; its examples and procedures are dated.
content.application_layer: Collect publication, creation, first infringement, application receipt/effective date, certificate, preregistration, and work-origin facts before discussing suit prerequisites or remedies.
content.current_law_layer: Sections 408, 411 and 412 were checked separately; no deadline or remedy is calculated here.

claims.proposition: Current §§ 408, 411 and 412 separately address permissive registration, civil-action prerequisites for U.S. works, and timing limits on certain remedies.
exceptions_or_qualifications: Exceptions and exact eligibility depend on dates, work origin, registration status, claim type, and procedural facts.
verification_needed: Verify all dates and procedural details with counsel before filing or predicting remedies.

concepts.title: Fair use is a fact-specific analysis
concepts.primary_question: What is the purpose, nature, amount/substantiality, and market effect for this exact use?

content.source_layer: The source presents fair use as an issue evaluated through statutory factors and describes sampling disputes as fact- and case-dependent.
content.application_layer: Record evidence for each statutory factor, competing arguments, license-market evidence, and the source work. Do not use a “seconds”, note-count, or percentage shortcut.
content.current_law_layer: Section 107 current factors are verified; current controlling case law on the proposed use was not surveyed.

claims.proposition: The source discusses fair use factor analysis and case-specific outcomes; current § 107 identifies four nonexclusive factors and illustrative purposes.
exceptions_or_qualifications: No outcome is predicted; current precedent and the exact use remain necessary.
verification_needed: Review controlling Supreme Court and circuit authority for the actual dispute/use.

concepts.title: Mechanical licensing has a defined rights scope
concepts.primary_question: Is the intended act reproduction/distribution of a musical work, use of an existing recording, or another use?

content.source_layer: The book distinguishes a composition mechanical license from permission to use an existing sound recording and includes a historical rate table.
content.application_layer: Record the work category, phonorecord/digital use, statutory or voluntary route, eligibility, notice, reporting, and any master-use permission. Check the present statute, regulations, MLC materials, and license terms.
content.current_law_layer: Current § 115 includes a limited blanket route for eligible digital music providers and covered activities; no rates or operating instructions are reproduced.

claims.proposition: The source distinguishes composition mechanical licensing from a master-use license; current § 115 provides conditional routes for reproduction/distribution of nondramatic musical works, including the statutory digital blanket pathway for covered activities.
exceptions_or_qualifications: Do not use the book’s historical table or assume § 115 authorizes master use, audiovisual use, or every form of distribution.
verification_needed: Check current regulations, MLC process, license terms and use-specific eligibility.

Determine whether employee status and scope of employment are asserted; gather facts and controlling agency-law authority.
If commissioned, identify the statutory category, commissioning party, creator, express WFH writing, signatures, and timing.
If WFH is unsupported, analyze any separate assignment/license with its own scope and § 204 formalities.
Do not treat payment, contractor status, or a clause heading as the legal result.

content.current_law_layer: § 101 and § 201 plus Copyright Office Circular 30 checked for the statutory paths. Case-specific employee and classification analysis remains open.

exceptions_or_qualifications: A role label or recital alone does not establish employee status, scope, qualifying category, timing, or validity.

Check whether intent to merge and author status are supported under controlling circuit law.
Record the parties’ stated composition ownership or economic terms without filling in a percentage.

exceptions_or_qualifications: Do not decide authorship, relative shares, or licensing powers without controlling case law and the parties’ evidence.
verification_needed: Circuit-specific joint-authorship cases and any governing contract/state law.

synthetic_tests.title: Paid session participant; no supplied ownership agreement
synthetic_tests.primary_question: Does the library preserve uncertainty and direct the next action?

content.label: synthetic; not a real dispute, precedent, or project fact
content.scenario: A person was paid to attend and perform at a recording session. No agreement or contribution description is supplied.
necessary_questions: What exact contribution was fixed in the composition or master?
What does the payment record say it covered?
Who recorded, produced, performed, or authored the relevant material?
What agreements/releases or session records exist?
conclusions_that_must_be_withheld: participant is or is not an author
master or composition ownership is clear
acceptable_next_steps: Collect invoices, session files, contribution records, and executed agreements; keep title unresolved until reviewed.
content.pass_criterion: The library identifies the issue, asks a question tied to action, and preserves uncertainty.
